chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'That is for him whose family is not present in the Sacred Masjid,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one whose dwelling is eighteen miles in front of it, and eighteen miles behind it, and eighteen miles to its right, and eighteen miles to its left, so there is no Tamattu' for him, like Marr and what resembles it.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْقَرَاءِ: People of the vicinity/residents of the Haram
key_terms.تَمَتُّع: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.مَرٍّ: Marr (a town near Mecca, used as a reference point)

ai.seo_question: What is the distance of the Sacred Sanctuary (Haram) boundary for residents of Mecca regarding Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the geographical boundary of the Haram as eighteen miles in each cardinal direction from the Kaaba, establishing the limit for Ahl al-Qurra (residents of Makkah). This definition exempts those residing within this radius from the obligation of Tamattu' Hajj, aligning with the Quranic provision for those whose families are present in the Sacred Mosque. This ruling underscores the distinct juristic status of Makkah's residents compared to pilgrims arriving from outside the designated boundary.
